seoTitle: Free Nginx Config Generator - Proxy, SPA, HTTPS
metaDescription: Generate Nginx server blocks for static sites, reverse proxy, single-page apps and HTTPS redirects, with optional gzip. Free, runs in your browser.
intro: Fill in a server name, root or upstream and a few options to get an Nginx server block for a static site, reverse proxy, SPA or plain HTTPS redirect.
why:
Nginx configuration is short but unforgiving. A missing semicolon, a try_files line that sends every URL to 404, or a proxy block without the forwarded headers can take a site down or break logins behind a proxy. Most setups repeat the same few patterns, so they are easy to get from a template.

This generator covers four: a static site with long-lived caching for assets, a single-page app that falls back to index.html, a reverse proxy to an upstream with the headers apps usually need, and a lone redirect from HTTP to HTTPS. You can add gzip settings and a certificate block that points at Let's Encrypt paths. Always run nginx -t before reloading. The text is generated in your browser.
howTo: Choose the type: static, reverse proxy, SPA or https redirect only.
Enter the server_name and, depending on the type, the root folder or the upstream address.
Tick HTTPS and gzip as needed.
Copy the config, test it with nginx -t and reload Nginx.

faq.q: Where do the certificate paths come from?
faq.a: With HTTPS ticked, the block points at /etc/letsencrypt/live/ followed by your server name for fullchain.pem and privkey.pem, the usual Certbot location. Change the paths if your certificates live elsewhere.

faq.q: What does the SPA option do differently?
faq.a: It sends any URL that is not a real file to /index.html, so client-side routes such as /dashboard load the app instead of returning 404. The static option returns 404 for missing files.

faq.q: Which headers does the reverse proxy add?
faq.a: Host, X-Real-IP, X-Forwarded-For and X-Forwarded-Proto, plus Upgrade and Connection settings so WebSocket connections can pass through. Adjust timeouts and buffering for heavy workloads.

faq.q: Is the output complete for production?
faq.a: It is a solid base but omits security headers, rate limits, TLS tuning and logging choices. Review those for your environment, and test the file before reloading.
